title: The uncomfortable: what to do when it surfaces

outline.heading: The thing that makes practice do anything at all
What showed up once somebody finally asked

points.text: Britton, Lindahl, Cooper, Canby and Palitsky (Clinical Psychological Science, 2021) — 96 participants in an eight-week programme, interviewed by an independent assessor on a 44-item instrument:
Goldberg, Lam, Britton and Davidson (Psychotherapy Research, 2022) — a US population sample, 434 people with meditation experience:
And one detail from there that is rarely retold: people who reported harm were just as glad they had practised as everyone else.
Matko and Van Dam (Current Opinion in Psychology, 2026)
Two conclusions are stable: unpleasant effects are common, and persistent harm is rare — on the order of a few per cent up to the mid-teens.

outline.heading: The window of tolerance — a second time, and not by accident

points.text: difficult experience inside the window is material. Difficult experience past the edge of the window is a signal to stop.
The last item is not "a reason to lower the dose" but a reason to leave the learning scenario immediately and reach a living person: a professional or a crisis line.

outline.heading: The words you explain difficulty to yourself with are an intervention

points.text: The paper "The roles and impacts of worldviews in the context of meditation-related challenges" (Transcultural Psychiatry, 2022) showed that the interpretive frame itself changes the trajectory and duration of difficulties.
When a session has rocked you but the stop signals haven't appeared, there are two working returns

outline.heading: Where to go if it persists beyond the session

points.text: If the heaviness reaches past the session and holds for several days, ease off practice and contact a living professional.
